title: Projective symmetry groups beyond spin-$1/2$: Classifying integer-spin quantum spin liquids
authors: Atanu Maity, Chunxiao Liu, Rhine Samajdar, Yasir Iqbal
abstract: Wen's projective symmetry group (PSG), introduced a quarter of a century ago, reduced the classification of symmetric quantum spin liquids to an algebraic problem and has guided the study of spin-$1/2$ models and materials ever since. Many current candidate materials and quantum simulators, however, have spin-$1$ or larger moments, and no comparable classification exists for them. We formulate the PSG for fermionic partons of arbitrary spin $S$. Integer and half-odd-integer spins already differ in their gauge structure. Half-odd-integer spins give the familiar $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $\mathrm{U}(1)$, and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant gauge groups, while integer spins give a different hierarchy that includes $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$; the latter has no spin-$1/2$ counterpart. Three lattice-independent results follow for integer spin. Singlet pairing of the partons is odd under site exchange. A lattice symmetry can exchange the particle and hole representations of the local constraint, which forces symmetry-related sites into opposite constraint sectors. And a time-reversal-symmetric $\mathrm{U}(1)$ state with the same constraint on every site can be gapped only if the number of sites per unit cell is a multiple of $2S+1$. We apply the formalism to the spin-$1$ diamond lattice, realized in frustrated A-site spinels, and find ten fully symmetric Ansätze up to second neighbors. In the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model at the mean-field level, the ground state depends on how the constraint is imposed. With the particle and hole representations, the lowest states are fully gapped $\mathrm{U}(1)$ states whose two sublattices sit in opposite constraint sectors, and one of them is gauge equivalent to a paired Ansatz. The classification provides a starting point for integer-spin quantum spin liquids on other lattices and in other materials.
summary: This paper generalizes the Projective Symmetry Group (PSG) classification method to quantum spin liquids with integer spins ($S \ge 1$). It establishes new symmetry constraints and reveals a distinct gauge structure for these higher-spin systems. The work provides a powerful theoretical framework for classifying and understanding the ground states of novel magnetic materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to extend the classification of symmetric quantum spin liquids (QSLs) beyond the well-studied spin-1/2 case to include systems with integer spins ($S=1, 2, \dots$).
main_result: A generalized Projective Symmetry Group (PSG) classification is formulated for arbitrary spin $S$, revealing a distinct hierarchy of invariant gauge groups for integer spins compared to half-odd-integer spins.
method: The methodology involves formulating the PSG for fermionic partons of spin $S$ and applying mean-field theory to analyze the resulting symmetry constraints.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum spin liquids described by spin-$S$ moments, analyzed using a fermionic parton representation and mean-field theory applied to lattice models like the spin-1 diamond lattice.
key_observables: The classification of PSGs, the gauge structure of the invariant gauge groups (e.g., U(1) $\ltimes$ Z2), and the existence of lattice-independent constraints (e.g., filling constraints for gapped U(1) states).
important_parameters: The spin quantum number $S$ (especially comparing $S=1/2$ to $S \ge 1$), and the ratio of exchange couplings in the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the fermionic parton representation and mean-field decoupling of the spin-rotation-invariant link variables.
figures_summary: The notes mention a Table IV summarizing short-range $Z_2 	imes Z_2$ Ansätze and their descendants, and a Figure illustrating the dependence of self-duality on the $J_2/J_1$ ratio.
paper_structure: The paper develops the PSG formalism for arbitrary spin $S$, derives lattice-independent constraints for integer spins, applies the formalism to specific lattices (like the spin-1 diamond lattice), and analyzes the resulting mean-field ground states.
why_interesting: The generalization of symmetry classification tools (like PSG) to higher-spin systems is crucial for understanding exotic magnetic phases in real materials, bridging abstract theory with complex condensed matter physics.
